# Cross-Entry Integration Checklist: Issues — creation, detail and editing

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements describing what this feature consumes from earlier entries, what it obliges them to deliver, and what four later entries will add to it, are complete, unambiguous and free of conflict — before the feature is decomposed into tasks
**Created**: 2026-08-31
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [contracts/](../contracts/) · [docs/ROADMAP.md](../../../docs/ROADMAP.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Provenance of the marks below**: every item was evaluated and marked by Claude on 2026-08-31, at the reviewer's explicit instruction to review the checklist, mark what was already true with citations, and apply the recommended fix to the rest. Each item carries its verdict: **Yes** means the requirement already satisfied the criterion and names where; **Fixed** means the specification was changed to satisfy it and names the change. A reviewer who disagrees with a verdict should uncheck that item — the citations are there to be argued with.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

This is a **requirements-quality** review, not a verification pass. Every item asks whether something is *written well*, not whether code *works*.

## Requirement Completeness — what this feature consumes

- [x] CHK001 Do the requirements distinguish the entries this feature **cannot be built without** from those it merely cites, rather than listing all of them in one dependency sentence? [Gap, Spec §Dependencies] — **Fixed**: *Dependencies* was rewritten around exactly that split: **Cannot be built without** (R1, R2, R5) and **Consumed but not blocking** (R3).
- [x] CHK002 Is each consumed contract named at the granularity its provider's author would need — the predicate, the counter row's shape, the route, the header slot — rather than by entry number alone? [Completeness, Spec §Dependencies] — **Fixed**: *Dependencies* now names what each contract must provide, and the new *Obligations this feature places on entries built before it* states the four unfixed ones in the form their provider's author needs.
- [x] CHK003 Are requirements stated for what this feature must do if a consumed contract arrives in a different shape than assumed — the counter's columns being the clearest case? [Gap, Spec §FR-013] — **Fixed**: *Obligations* closes with the rule: this feature follows the shape that exists rather than changing it, and the divergence is recorded as an amendment.
- [x] CHK004 Is the module this feature extracts identified by something an R5 author could act on, given that R5 is unbuilt and its file layout is undecided? [Gap, Spec §FR-044] — **Fixed**: *Obligations* names the module by its rule rather than its path — it stays inside R5's feature until this feature moves it — which is actionable before R5's layout exists.
- [x] CHK005 Are the constraints this feature adds to a table another entry owns stated as requirements, or left to be discovered when the migration is written? [Gap, Spec §FR-005] — **Fixed**: `FR-005` states it as a requirement on this feature, and *Obligations* names it so R5's author is not surprised to find another entry altering their table.

## Requirement Consistency — the dependency claims

- [x] CHK006 Does the stated dependency set agree with the set the requirements actually exercise — is every entry listed as a dependency genuinely required, and is none required but unlisted? [Conflict, Spec §Dependencies] — **Fixed**: *Dependencies* resolves it: R3 is consumed but not blocking, because the deactivation flag is a column on R1's `user` table. The correction is recorded in the section itself.
- [x] CHK007 Do the requirements agree with the roadmap's own dependency edge for this entry, and is any divergence recorded as a reconciliation rather than left implicit? [Consistency, Spec §Dependencies, Roadmap §R6] — **Yes**: The roadmap's R6 row depends on R5, and the spec's chain runs through it; the only divergence — R3's status — is now recorded rather than implicit.
- [x] CHK008 Is the claim that this feature is the markdown subset's second call site consistent with every other statement about the subset's ownership, including the roadmap's? [Consistency, Spec §FR-044, §Reconciliations, Roadmap §1.1] — **Yes**: The markdown reconciliation states both readings and why both hold, and cites roadmap §1.1 by name.
- [x] CHK009 Are the requirements that reach into another entry's work consistent about who performs the reach — this feature, or the entry being reached into? [Consistency, Spec §FR-028, §FR-044] — **Yes**: `FR-028` and `FR-044` both put the reach on this feature; *Obligations* says why R5 cannot perform either.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK010 Is "every project-scoped screen that exists when this feature lands" resolvable to a definite set, or does it depend on a build order the requirements do not fix? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-028] — **Fixed**: `FR-028` and the header reconciliation now name the definite set of three: project details, issue detail and create issue, the board being R10's.
- [x] CHK011 Is "the destination MUST be a route that exists when this feature lands" stated as a constraint on this feature or as an assumption about another? [Clarity, Spec §FR-060] — **Yes**: `FR-060` states it as a MUST on this feature — the destination must be a route that exists when it lands — not as an assumption about R5.
- [x] CHK012 Is "adding no dependency" specific about which dependency ledger it refers to, and about whether an already-installed transitive package counts as added? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-044] — **Fixed**: `FR-044` now names the ledger — `AGENTS.md`'s approved table — and rules that a package present on disk counts as added the moment this feature imports it directly.
- [x] CHK013 Is "promoted out of R5's feature directory" precise about the destination, or only about the origin? [Clarity, Spec §FR-044] — **Fixed**: `FR-044` now names the destination: the shared location the repository reserves for code with a real second use, referenced from there rather than re-exported.

## Requirement Completeness — what later entries add

- [x] CHK014 Is each of the four later entries' additions described precisely enough that its author could implement it without re-deriving the contract from this feature's code? [Completeness, Spec §Reconciliations, contracts/mutators.md] — **Fixed**: The R11 reconciliation now states `OT-OPS-016`'s gate in full, so R11's author need not re-derive it.
- [x] CHK015 Are requirements stated for how each cascade arm attaches, distinctly from what each arm removes? [Completeness, Spec §FR-059] — **Fixed**: `FR-059` separates the two: the arm is a property of the referencing table's own declaration, and each of the four arms is assigned to exactly one entry.
- [x] CHK016 Is the obligation on later entries to extend the delete confirmation's stated size stated as a requirement on them, or only as a description of what will happen? [Clarity, Spec §FR-062] — **Yes**: `FR-062` states it as a MUST on them: each later entry that attaches rows to the cascade adds its own count to this confirmation.
- [x] CHK017 Are requirements stated for whether this feature's own acceptance scenarios must continue to hold after each later entry reaches back into its mutators? [Gap] — **Fixed**: The reach-back reconciliation now requires every scenario and criterion here to hold after each reach-back, and makes a break a defect in the reaching entry.
- [x] CHK018 Is the decision to build no extension points stated as a requirement with a rationale, so a later planner cannot read it as an oversight? [Completeness, Spec §Out of Scope] — **Yes**: *Out of Scope* states it with the rationale from Principles I, III and VI, so it reads as a decision rather than an omission.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK019 Is the criterion that another entry's scenarios pass unchanged after the extraction verifiable, given that those scenarios may themselves change before this feature lands? [Measurability, Assumption, Spec §SC-017] — **Fixed**: `SC-017` now pins it to the scenarios R5 holds *at the moment the extraction runs*, and says the licence is to move the module, not to adjust the tests.
- [x] CHK020 Is there a measurable criterion for the mutator contracts later entries depend on, verifiable on this feature alone before any of them exists? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-018] — **Yes**: `SC-018` says so in its own words: both verifiable on this feature alone, before any later entry reaches back.
- [x] CHK021 Can "one implementation renders both" be objectively verified from the requirements, without inspecting the module layout? [Measurability, Spec §SC-017] — **Yes**: `SC-017`'s first clause is observable from the two screens — identical source renders identically — without inspecting any module layout.

## Scenario Coverage & Boundaries

- [x] CHK022 Are requirements defined for the case where this feature is built before an entry it depends on — or is that ordering excluded, and stated as excluded? [Gap, Spec §Dependencies] — **Fixed**: *Dependencies* now states that building before R2 or R5 is not a supported ordering, and why no reduced version exists.
- [x] CHK023 Is every item deferred to a later entry attributed to exactly one entry, with no capability claimed by two or left unclaimed? [Consistency, Spec §Out of Scope] — **Yes**: Each of the eleven *Out of Scope* bullets names exactly one owning entry, or records the item as out of v1 entirely.
- [x] CHK024 Does the scope boundary agree with the roadmap's own R6 row in both directions — nothing in scope that the roadmap defers, nothing deferred that the roadmap assigns here? [Consistency, Spec §Out of Scope, Roadmap §R6] — **Yes**: Checked against the roadmap's R6 row in both directions: every *In* item appears, every *Deferred* item is deferred, and the two cross-cutting requirements added here apply R2's and §7's conventions rather than claiming them.
- [x] CHK025 Are the requirements this feature places on entries that are already specified but unbuilt recorded where those entries' authors will encounter them, rather than only here? [Traceability, Gap] — **Fixed**: *Obligations* is the list, and entry R5's own specification now carries a pointer to it in its *Dependencies* section.

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK026 Are the inherited constraints distinguished from the decisions this feature makes, clearly enough that a reviewer does not attribute an inherited rule to this entry? [Clarity, Spec §Inherited constraints] — **Yes**: *Inherited constraints, not decisions this specification makes* is a section of its own, listing five inherited rules.
- [x] CHK027 Is each assumption about another entry's behaviour stated with the consequence of it being wrong, rather than as a bare assertion? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions] — **Fixed**: Each silent-source default now carries an **If wrong** clause naming the cost, and the concurrency default was promoted out of the list into `FR-064`.
- [x] CHK028 Are the dependency-approval obligations this feature triggers — any package it must install, and any it must decline — stated in the requirements, or discovered only at planning? [Gap, Spec §FR-040, §FR-044] — **Fixed**: *Dependencies* now closes with **Dependency approval this feature triggers**: the ordering library is already approved and needs installation only, and nothing else here may add a package.

## Notes

- Every item is marked; see **Provenance of the marks** above for who marked them and what each verdict means
- Uncheck any item whose verdict you disagree with — each carries the citation it rests on
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- CHK006 and CHK001 pointed at the same sentence and are closed together: *Dependencies* now splits **cannot be built without** (R1, R2, R5) from **consumed but not blocking** (R3), and records the correction explicitly rather than leaving two documents to disagree
- CHK025 was the one item that could not be closed inside this feature's own documents. It is now closed by a pointer added to entry R5's specification, in its *Dependencies* section, naming the four contracts R6 needs from it — the only edit this pass made outside `specs/006-…/`
